analyst_estimate_revisions.note: Confirmed via alpha_db.py correlate: all these fields produce daily-return correlation 0.88-1.00 with each other. Best result across this whole cluster was Sharpe 1.02 (rank(ts_zscore(anl4_fs_detail_estimates_basic_qf_v4_nd_div_std, 15))), which still failed BRAIN's real submission threshold (LOW_SHARPE limit=1.25) and LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE. Treat as one used-up idea, not several.

operating_income_small_cap_dependent.note: group_rank(-ts_delta(operating_income, N), subindustry) achieves strong headline Sharpe (1.8-1.96 across windows 3/5/8) but FAILS LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE every time, even after trying 3 different cap-tilting approaches (rank(cap) multiply after group_rank, weighting before group_rank, and trade_when(rank(cap)>0.5,...) restricting to only the top-cap half). The check's limit itself scales down with headline Sharpe (~0.3-0.4x), so tilting doesn't fix the ratio - this looks like a structural property of the field (operating income changes are likely more informative for smaller, less-covered companies) rather than a weighting bug. Not worth further tilting attempts on this specific field - the core idea is real but not BRAIN-submittable as constructed. A genuinely different field is needed, not more variants of this one.
failed_approaches: cap_multiply (rank(cap) after outer group_rank - actively hurts, Sharpe drops to 0.2-0.3)
cap_weighted_before_rank (rank(cap) multiplied into the inner expression before group_rank - re-normalization washes it out)
cap_trade_when_top_half (trade_when(rank(cap)>0.5,...) - still fails, limit scales down with Sharpe)

authorized_option_shares_concentration.note: rank(-ts_delta(authorized_option_shares_outstanding_count, 20)) with SUBINDUSTRY neutralization achieves strong Sharpe (1.5-1.7, Fitness 2.2-2.8) and even PASSES LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE at baseline truncation (0.08) - a genuine improvement over the operating_income cluster. But it FAILS CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT every time (~0.45-0.49 vs limit 0.10), and three different fix approaches all failed to move that number: lowering truncation (0.08->0.02/0.04, barely changed it: 0.477->0.457), ts_backfill smoothing the sparse field (destroyed Sharpe down to 0.93-1.05, no concentration improvement), and ts_decay_linear-smoothing the delta over several days (Sharpe held at 1.62 but concentration still 0.49 AND newly broke LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE too, which had been passing). Working hypothesis (not directly confirmed - a coverage diagnostic was skipped): this field likely has sparse data coverage (not every company reports option-share authorizations), so the real tradeable universe is a narrow subset of TOP3000, which structurally forces concentration regardless of how the delta/timing is smoothed. If revisited later, check field coverage/NaN rate first before trying more smoothing variants - that's the untested diagnostic that would confirm or rule out this hypothesis.
failed_approaches: ts_backfill(field, 60/120) before delta - destroyed Sharpe (1.71->0.93-1.05), concentration unchanged
ts_decay_linear(ts_delta(field,20), 5-20) smoothing - held Sharpe at 1.62 but concentration still failed AND broke LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE which had been passing

live_saturated_ratios.note: Confirmed via audit_portfolio.py running real PnL correlation across all 16 currently-ACTIVE alphas (not just one batch). These field/ratio families each already have a live alpha and should NOT be resubmitted in any window/template variant - not because they failed, but because a correlated sibling is already active and would likely be blocked by SELF_CORRELATION or, per the competition's actual rules, risks looking like deliberate noise/gaming if stacked further. Also notable: fn_debt_instrument_face_amount_a (raw) correlated 0.70 with anl4_bvps_flag - two fields from completely different datasets - suggesting fundamental ratios broadly may share more hidden common-factor exposure than field names imply. Prefer genuinely different DATA TYPES (price/volume techniques, news/sentiment vectors) over more fundamental ratios for real diversification from here.
